subject.title: feat(feeds): expose publisher follow gateway RPCs

question: Should signed publisher-feed following become a permanent OpenClaw core gateway/CLI/storage capability, or should it be implemented as a ClawHub/OpenClaw plugin using existing extension seams?
rationale: The branch is technically substantial but establishes new core RPC, scheduler, SQLite, configuration-consumption, and trust-root contracts; repository policy cannot resolve that product boundary without explicit ownership intent.

options.title: Route through a plugin
options.body: Keep ClawHub-specific feed logic outside core and add only any narrowly proven generic RPC, lifecycle, or storage seam that the plugin API lacks.

options.title: Sponsor the core stack
options.body: Accept core ownership, then require the full stacked series, public docs, generated client follow-through, security review, and fresh/upgrade/live proof before merge.

options.title: Pause the feed program
options.body: Leave the draft stack open or close it without landing until the producer RFC and long-term ownership model are approved.

recommendation.title: Route through a plugin
recommendation.body: Keep ClawHub-specific feed logic outside core and add only any narrowly proven generic RPC, lifecycle, or storage seam that the plugin API lacks.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history shows the strongest connection to gateway method ownership, authentication, discovery, and protocol evolution.
